jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Specific Reading
jokes.joke: I went to a fortune teller who also worked for the mob. She held my palm and said, “I see a long journey, a sudden disappearance, and your family never finding the body.” I said, “That’s incredibly specific.” She said, “It’s not a prediction. You still owe Tony three grand.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: The Palm Reader
jokes.joke: I went to a fortune teller and she grabbed my palm, looked real deep into it, and said, 'I sense... you don't trust me.' And I said, 'Lady, you're holding my hand and reading it like a used car history report, of course I don't trust you.' She goes, 'Fine, I also sense you're going to leave a bad review.' I said, 'Now THAT one I believe.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Crystal Ball
jokes.joke: I went to a psychic last week, and immediately I got suspicious because before she even touched the crystal ball, she asked me for my name. Lady, you’re supposed to tell me the future, and you don’t even know who just walked through your bead curtain? I gave her a fake name just to test her, and five minutes later she looked deep into my palm and said, 'Sir, you have deep trust issues.'

jokes.title: Backyard Mob
jokes.joke: I think organised crime has moved into my backyard. It's the raccoons. There's a clear hierarchy—the big guy never leaves the deck, the others do all the dirty work tipping the cans. When I tried to stop them, the leader just stared at me and said, 'We know where you live. Leave the trash, and nobody gets hurt.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Backyard Prophecies
jokes.joke: I once hired this backyard psychic because she said she could read my aura. Halfway through, she leaned in and whispered, “I sense someone close to you is hiding something.” I said, “Yeah, it’s you. You showed up with a crystal ball and a Venmo request.”

scores.comment: Clean and readable with a solid callback, but the suspicious-customer/psychic premise is fairly expected and the final turn is more amusing than strong.
Good escalation from testing the psychic to accidentally validating her diagnosis. The final line lands cleanly and retroactively strengthens the setup.
Clear visual premise and natural seed integration, but raccoons-as-mafia is familiar and the final threat mostly completes the expected analogy rather than sharply overturning it.
Concise setup and a decent transactional punchline, but 'backyard psychic' clearly introduces a third seed concept, so prompt fit must be capped despite otherwise competent construction.
Sharp misdirection from prediction to debt collection; clean punchline lands well.
Decent setup but the closing line just restates suspicion rather than escalating it.
Fun raccoon-mafia conceit with a solid capper, though the middle sags slightly.
Venmo turn is amusing and current, but a touch predictable as psychic-scam jokes go.
Crisp economy and a well-timed punchline, though the mob-prediction turn is a familiar comic premise.
Natural conversational cadence, but the 'bad review' payoff lands more like an observational shrug than a sharp turn.
Raccoons acting like mobsters is a well-worn trope, and having the raccoon speak breaks the stand-up reality without a strong laugh payoff.
Competent punchline, but it introduces Backyard alongside Fortune Teller and Suspicious, violating the two-concept restriction.
Clean mob-debt turn lands with solid timing and a strong final line.
Serviceable distrust bit; used-car line helps but overall mild.
Name-test setup builds cleanly to a competent trust-issues snap.
Venmo punch is fine but excess seed concepts (backyard + psychic + suspicion) tank fit.
Clean mob‑fortune teller angle; solid turn, moderately funny.
Decent premise; predictable turn and lighter payoff.
Clear setup; familiar suspicion beat, mild humor.
